name: My Safety Plan
careNote: Handle with care. This app is a suicide-prevention safety plan, made by Daraja Studio in memory of Jerry's son Ryan. In this test you are NOT writing about yourself. You play a counselor showing how the plan works, and you type only the made-up example words given to you. If anything in this test brings up hard feelings for you, stop at any time — that is completely fine. You can call or text 988 (the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) any time, day or night, and in an emergency call 911.

persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Mrs. Carter, a retired school counselor who now trains church volunteers in Illinois. Tomorrow you will show the volunteers how a safety plan works, so today you are filling in a pretend example plan for a made-up teenager called Jake. Nothing you type is about you or anyone real.

challenge.intro: You are Mrs. Carter, the counselor, making a pretend example plan for a made-up teenager called Jake. Type ONLY the example words given here — nothing about yourself. The app is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open My Safety Plan with the normal link (not a 🧪 test copy). If a welcome card shows, tap 'I’ll look around myself'. Scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK. The plan is now empty.

tasks.text: Add two warning signs for Jake: "stops replying to messages" and "stays in bed all day".
tasks.hint: Warning signs are in the first step of the tab where the plan is written. Each sign goes on its own line — look for the way to add another line.

tasks.text: Add two things Jake can do on his own to feel a little safer: "listen to music" and "walk around the park".
tasks.hint: This is step 2 — things he can do ON HIS OWN, without contacting anyone. One idea per line.

tasks.text: Add one person Jake can ask for help: his uncle "Uncle Mike", phone 847-555-0100 (a pretend number).
tasks.hint: People who can help go in step 4. Each person needs BOTH a name and a phone number.

tasks.text: Add a second helpline under the 988 one: "Crisis Text Line", number 741741 (you text the word HOME to it).
tasks.hint: Helplines and counselors go in step 5, Professionals. Add a new line under the 988 one that is already there, and check every digit of 741741.

tasks.text: Write Jake's one thing most worth living for: "my little sister Emma". Then make sure the plan is saved and shows on the My plan tab.
tasks.hint: It is the very last line in the place where the plan is written, after step 6. Then use the Save button.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: a plan written on a calmer day for a very hard moment
warning signs, things that help, and people and helplines to contact
private, kept on the phone, open it and follow the steps

lines: Welcome. This video explains My Safety Plan, gently and in plain words. If you need someone right now, Talk to someone now, at the bottom, calls nine-eight-eight.
First, what a safety plan is. Sometimes a person goes through a very hard time, and may even have thoughts of ending their life. Then it is very hard to think clearly.
A safety plan is a short list, written on a calmer day, of what helps. When a hard moment comes, you do not have to think. You open the plan and follow it.
Counselors and doctors use this kind of plan. The app follows a well-known method called Stanley-Brown safety planning.
It is for anyone who has hard days, and for the people who love them.
Daraja Studio made this app in memory of Ryan.
Let us look at the screen. At the top is the name, and a small lock. It says private, stays on this device.
Under it are three tabs: My plan, Build, edit, and Right now.
Build, edit is where the plan is written. Six short steps and one last line. You type a few words in each.
Step one is my warning signs. Signs that a hard time is starting. For example, I stop answering texts.
Step two is things I can do on my own to feel a little safer. For example, a walk, a cold shower, or music.
Step three is people and places that take my mind off it. Not to talk about the problem, just to be around life.
Step four is people I can ask for help. A name and a phone number. People who will pick up.
Step five is professionals and agencies, like a counselor or a doctor. The nine-eight-eight Lifeline is already filled in.
Step six is making my environment safer: putting distance between you and things you could be hurt with.
The last line is the one thing most worth living for, in your own words. It shows first when the plan opens.
To add a line, tap plus add another. When you finish, tap Save my plan. It also keeps every word as you type.
My plan shows the finished plan, easy to read on a hard day. Each person you added gets a Call button.
Right now is for a hard moment. First, an honest check-in. Tap a face. Nobody sees it but you.
Then breathe with the circle. Tap Start one minute, and breathe in as it grows and out as it shrinks.
Below that, your reasons for staying, the things that have helped before, and the people you can reach, each with a Call button.
Now the most important part. Talk to someone now calls nine-eight-eight, the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. Free, confidential, day or night, in the US.
Under it, more ways to reach out: text nine-eight-eight, emergency nine-one-one, the Veterans line, Spanish, and seven-one-one for deaf or hard of hearing.
You will reach a real, trained person. It is okay to call just to talk. Outside the US, the app points to findahelpline dot com.
How to start. On a calm day, open Build, edit and write the first three steps. Come back for the rest.
Then show your plan to one person you trust. If you love someone who struggles, fill it out together. That is why this app exists.
It is completely private. It stays only on this phone, with no account, and nothing is sent anywhere. Save a copy, at the bottom, makes a backup file.
My Safety Plan is free, and always will be. It is a tool to keep your plan close, not therapy, and not a substitute for emergency help.
The question mark button in the corner has the tour and help any time. Take it slowly.

daily.task: Read your plan in My Safety Plan and add or change one line — for example one thing that helps you feel calm.
